newsitem.title: USA: CBOT wheat closes lower on profit taking, soybeans.
newsitem.headline: CBOT wheat closes lower on profit taking, soybeans.

text.p: CBOT wheat futures closed lower on speculative profit taking and on a drop in soybeans, traders said.

CBOT wheat moved lower despite concern about flooding in the U.S. spring wheat growing region but that activity had more of an impact on the Minneapolis Grain Exchange spring wheat contract, the traders said.

"Spring flooding potentially would help wheat but it was mostly in the MGE market because of flood potential in the spring areas," said Vic Lespinasse of Dean Witter. MGE spring wheat futures Monday gained on spreads with CBOT wheat.
Most traders said the CBOT soft red winter contracts were lower because the market was overbought during Friday's rally and was undergoing a profit-taking setback.
LIT America sold 1.5 million bushels of July and Rosenthal Collins sold two million bushels of July, traders said.

Friday's Commodity Futures Trading Commission Commitments of Traders report held few surprises for the market. The CFTC said as of Tuesday, funds were long wheat by roughly 54 million bushels and short about 81.8 million bushels.
Wheat closed two to 7-1/2 cents per bushel lower, with March down seven at $3.76-1/4 and May was down six at $3.81.

Position squaring was noted in the March before expiration of that contract slated for 1201 CST Wednesday. But traders said the expiration should be quiet because the open interest in the March has been drawn down sharply. CBOT preliminary figures early Monday showed the open interest in the March wheat contract at 835,000 contracts.

Little direction came from USDA's weekly export inspections report. USDA early Monday said 12.707 million bushels of U.S. wheat were inspected for export during the week ended March 13. The market was expecting from 12 million to 14 million bushels.
Technicians early Monday cited first support in the May at $3.80 and second support at $3.66-1/2. The session low for May was $3.80.
First resistance in the May was $3.93-1/2 and second resistance was at $4.07. The session high for May was $3.91.
The four- and 20-day moving averages were giving off bullish signals early Monday.
The nine-day relative strength index (RSI) in the May closed at 60.6 percent. The market generally considers an RSI of 70 or more as overbought and 30 or less as oversold.

ADM Investor Services bought two million bushels of July, Refco Inc bought 1.5 million bushels of May, Rosenthal Collins sold two million bushels of July and LIT America sold 2.5 million bushels of July, traders said.
Wheat futures volume was estimated by the CBOT at 18,000 contracts, below the 20,528 traded Friday.

In wheat options, FIMAT Futures bought 300 May $3.50 puts at two cents and sold 300 May $3.80 puts at 10 cents, traders said. Cargill Investor Services bought 200 July $3.70 calls, sold 200 July $4.00 calls and sold 200 July $3.60 puts at three cents, traders said.
Wheat options volume was estimated at 4,000 contracts, below the 8,153 traded Friday.
